item.title: Re: Threadmother (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, Spinner wasn't an optimal suggestion, also makes too many allusions to something spider-like, which isn't quite the case. I really liked Threadmother because it gives a bit of a warmer feel to the entity, it doesn't seem ominous or threatening. Other ideas I had was "Auditor" (someone who listens), "The Braided Idol", "Harmony" and "Sonority of Concord".

About the Sumerian link, I honestly thought that I would invent that part, and for the later parts I have historical images to use.

I've also got a good friend who's an illustrator who's making an image to use, so I'll use his as the main image, and then some images from greek/roman/norse mythology.

Francesca is a researcher yes, but the reason that it's done through interviews is because her logs haven't allowed the Foundation to do what she's done with the SCP. The Foundation is trying to figure out if she's deliberately withholding something from them, or what the reason is that they can't reproduce her results.

I have a very specific end in mind. My idea is that Francesca got her interest in musical theory in her childhood, hiding in her room she would put on music when things got too bad to drown out the sounds around her. The many hours she spent with the music developed her interest, which later became her profession.

In the end, an administrator and a number of researchers visit the site, having a heated discussion in glass room next to Threadmother about what to do with the SCP. Some are arguing for the destruction of the SCP. Francesca hears their heated argument, goes over to a stereo in the cave and puts on music to shield Threadmother from the argument, just as she used music to shield herself from her parents arguing. And that's the end.

(sidenote, they actually end up not destroying the SCP, but decide to have a smaller team run the site with Francesca as leader).

item.title: Questions about SCP Content on Twitch.tv and more
item.content:encoded:
Hey! I recently came up with an idea for a SCP Article and Concept that I don't think has ever been done before and isn't really covered in the wiki's legal guidelines.

Essentially I want to create a VTuber (Virtual YouTuber or Twitch Streamer) to stream on Twitch with. VTuber's are generally 3D models that are rigged to react to the operator's movements and emotions. I wanted to create one based off of a SCP article (That i am currently writing) which would be useed as his backstory.

For more information on the Concept: VTuber SCP Concept

So…. I have a lot of questions…

Questions about Twitch Licensing and Credits:
1. Since the Character I would be streaming as is based on a SCP Article which falls under SCPwiki’s CC Licensing, I would assume the content I produce would need to fall under that same License? If so, I'm not sure how to set that up with twitch as I'm not entirely sure what their content falls under.

2. With the Character being an original creation of mine, would I still need to link to it’s article page and the Author (Me) for credit? Or would just linking to the SCPwiki be sufficient?

3. What rules and/or limitations (if any) would I need to abide by in my content since twitch is an Offsite platform? Examples: 1. Would I be able to stream myself as this character playing a game? even though the game may fall under a different license than CC? 2. As a musician, would I be able to cover copyrighted songs? (provided I follow twitch’s guidelines concerning music as well)

Questions about the Model:
I created the Model and Name before I had the idea to make it a SCP. In that case, would the model (including related images) and name still belong to me, but just be used on the wiki and on stream with my permission? Or would the model and name need to be under CC as well?

Not all of the content being producing would be directly related to the SCP universe, but if the character is connected, I'm not sure what limitations and restrictions would be applied

I love the SCP Universe and don't want to do anything that would be against their guidelines, nor do I want to incur the wrath of a DMCA Take down.

In closing I have no idea what I am doing lol, and any legal help or advice is extremely appreciated!

(There are probably many things that I have not thought of and many questions may rise up. if you have any questions or suggestions of other questions I should be asking, please let me know)

[[/collapsible]]

item.title: To grandiose for my own good
item.content:encoded:
Man, when I first discovered scp, i was awful at writing. At the best of times you'd get an incoherent mess that completely defied things such as tone, theme, plot, and grammar. Now, if I sit down and write a story, it will at least make sense grammatically.

I mean, in my head i can craft a coherent story, but ideas don't mean [REDACTED] to be honest, the biggest struggle I've faced when joining the scp community, (aside from biting the bullet and dealing with the garbage interface that is wikidot) has been coming up with an idea I'm ok with throwing into the kindling. By that, I mean an idea which i don't think i could expand upon further when i improve in skill.

It's difficult to find someone who shares my struggle. I don't suffer from a lack of ideas. I don't suffer from a lack of effort. I struggle from being to picky. I have a plethora of ideas I wish to spew upon paper, but I just don't feel I'm sufficiently skilled enough to do them justice.

And I'm stuck in this purgatory of coming up with an idea that I'm ok with letting go of. I have so many ideas for scp as a whole, not just anomalous objects, I'm talking tales, GOI's, canons, and so much more. I guess I'm just frustrated that I'm not confident enough in my skull to allow myself to write what I want.

item.title: The Friendly Shadow
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional

Elevator Pitch: A sentient, living shadow, who belongs to a man named Clarence.

Central Narrative: It revolves around the wholesome relationship between Clarence and his Shadow.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I'm unsure if these listed below make the SCP unique on the site, but I hope this is what you meant by Hook or Attention Grabber. Just yell out if you want me to edit this.

  1. It's a sentient shadow (Most Shadow related SCPs I've researched have limited sentience or are just furniture)
  2. It's unclear on whether Clarence is anomaly, the shadow, or just both.

Additional Notes:

+ The Friendly Shadow's Quirk Ideas
- Close

Whether these are a good ideas or not is why I'm putting these here. Yell out if any seem good or bad. I always like to hear feedback and opinions.

  1. I was thinking that the shadow could move off of Clarence and interact with other shadows of people and objects.
  2. The shadow can talk to Clarence and others telepathically
  3. The shadow can only talk to Clarence
+ Expanding on the Narrative
- Close

As you probably saw above, I'm hoping to let this be emotional. I want a rather wholesome attachment with Clarence and his shadow. They have known of each other since childhood. It's not some recent anomaly. Below are a few extra ideas which I would like critique for. I was planning on doing one, but decided to keep my options open for the critters who have been doing this much longer then myself.

  1. The shadow is a parasite and is detrimental to Charles's health whether either of them know or not.
  2. Forces wish for the shadow to leave Clarence and both protest.
+ The Inspiration
- Close

For those who are as nerdy as me, the inspiration behind this was three things specifically.

  1. The Movie which has yet to (or may never) be released, Me and My Shadow. Note: If you've seen or are about to look up what this is, you'll know this had the biggest impact of the three.
  2. Peter Pan and his shadow
  3. Doctor Who, Season 4, Episode 8, Silence in the Library.

Let me know what can be used (if anything can be). Can't wait to hear from you. -Cope

item.title: Re: The "Uncontainable" SCP
item.content:encoded:
So, like others have said before (above) the anomaly seems intended to make this person hard to contain. Which isn't super believable, as it seems like a gimmick to make it more dramatic.

Additionally, I don't understand why the Foundation would hire him at all. Or why they wouldn't just amnesticize him concerning the ability and his history with Chicago Spirit, then give him another identity and put him under surveillance.

Moreover, if they decided to contain him they could go in nontraditional methods: keeping him in a medically induced coma, containing him outdoors after amnesticizing him so that he lived a rural life on a farm somewhere or a mountain cabin and having him surveilled, or trying SRA's to negate his anomalous ability (as you mentioned they originated from his contact with something reality bending).

Finally, even if none of the above was effective or was just forgotten about for the moment… I don't know why the Foundation would consistently bail him out for bad petty crimes he tries to commit on the side… or even WHY he was trying to do so.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: The "Uncontainable" SCP

As a general note, minutiae information like containment chamber size (which unless it's rather pertinent to containment success, isn't a requirement by any means) or height (which can vary over time anyway) tend to not be aspects that will change a reader's vote. It can be good to have to help a reader better visualize the anomaly and containment, but the author should also be mindful of not getting bogged down in excessive specifics.

item.title: Re: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look.

+ show block
– hide block

I'm admittedly not a huge fan of the general premise, mostly because I can't see the Foundation testing the item repeatedly (if it's clear that just grabbing the thing will cause the effect to manifest, which will cost the life of whoever did the grabbing, the Foundation has no reason not to lock it up to avoid accidents) and the GOC raid feels contrived and gratuitous in how it conveniently complicates matters to force the rest of the story to happen. Also, as someone who headcanons the Foundation as being extremely competent, the repeated "claiming" of agents breaks my suspension of disbelief as a reader. Both narrative approaches (GoI intervention, Foundation repeatedly failing to contain the anomaly) are also pretty commonly used; I personally would like to see a more unique story set up.

The core anomaly of "item overrides a person's identity" is already well-explored in articles like Bright's amulet (SCP-963 "Immortality") and the more benign SCP-1510 ("The Tarnished Legionnaire"). Both of those articles also have some backstory regarding the reason for manifestation of the anomaly; 963 implies that there was an activation process necessary to empower the amulet, and 1510 has an interview that details a curse placed on the individual whose identity overrides the wearers of the helmet. Are there plans for exploring why this backpack behaves the way it does? That is, why it effectively steals the lives of uninvolved people, and allows the guy to live in blissful ignorance of the harm that's been done?

I can see this maybe working as a sort of urban horror piece if you characterize the guy as being more on the selfish side and being fully aware of how his backpack's ability messes with other people. You could potentially add a more complex motive than just "wants to fulfill his dream"—have him be aware that he was killed before because of people who mugged him, have him attach a watch to his backpack so he can time his next "death" in a place filled with crime, and so on. Then he's not only getting to explore the world on stolen time, he's also (in his mind, anyway) getting back at all the robbers who have taken things that don't belong to them.

And then I would go further with a twist of some kind: maybe the Foundation catches the guy and lies to him about the backpack getting picked up by a kid in a poor neighborhood in the exact same situation: wanted to explore the world, felt trapped, etc. The guy realizes that it's very likely that he's hurt more innocent people out there during his travels. He asks the researchers for the means to collect his memoirs/write an explorers' guide, and then realizes he won't have time to finish compiling his work into a book. He asks if there's anyone out there suffering a terminal illness or the like whom he can possibly get one more week from so he has something lasting to give to the world. The Foundation states that if a suitable candidate is found, they will allow another manifestation. The article ends noting that the team are still deciding whether it's prudent to honor the entity's request for another manifestation. Your decision on whether or not the Foundation publishes the book of Charles's memoirs.

Anyway, that's how I personally would approach it. You definitely don't need to use the same story beats, but in general this is what I would like to see:

  • more relatable, in-depth motivation/characterization for Charles
  • a more unique narrative structure with fewer contrived plot points
  • competent Foundation handling of the anomaly
  • an "ending note" that sticks with the reader (for my setup, it would be the inherent question of "if you were on the research team, would you honor the entity's request for one last manifestation?")

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

This is my first SCP and I'm really happy with how its turned out so far.

SCP-XXXX: Thermites
Word Count: 3,823
Greenlit post: http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13365263/scp-idea:thermites
Draft: http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/cloudncali

Looking forward to what the community thinks.

This article started as a silly twist on the word thermite (the pyrotechnic powder) actually being Thermal Termites. The narrative developed from my fondness of SCPs with more human elements. The SCP Foundation is full of people from different backgrounds, its always fun to see different personalities show through the cold and stiff atmosphere of the foundation.

item.title: Re: mysterious blackmail
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look. As a general note, your concept post has a lot of simple errors like missing punctuation and run-on sentences. This automatically makes me as a reviewer hesitant to want to give a greenlight, as I am uncertain as to whether the draft would be written to the expected clinical tone standards for the mainsite.

+ show block
– hide block

So far as content goes, I'm not a fan of the premise since it relies heavily on a compulsion effect, which is one of the oldest anomalous shortcuts on the site. As a general note, the "it makes you crazy/act a very specific way" approach isn't particularly interesting on its own anymore, given how many times SCPs with that effect have been written. Take a look at the articles tagged with "compulsion". Typically, an SCP object's effect forcing someone to do something tends to come off as a lazy or contrived narrative, since there's more genuine tension if there's a struggle involved, and/or if the people instead act of their own volition rather than just because the author needs them to for the story to work. Consider reading through the further discussion on the narrative issues of compulsion and addiction effects.

The details about the anomaly are also kind of strange. The phrasing of "all sentient organisms", for example. Dogs, cats, and even lobsters are considered sentient. I presume none of them can donate though? Also, the "go to your nearest charity" bit doesn't quite make sense since not all charity organizations have easily accessible buildings (some charities set up donation drop boxes for things like used clothes and toys, and others have someone with a desk and box sitting in front of a grocery store). The fact that the type of money rarely changes implies that the anomaly is solely affecting countries that use the US dollar/people who have access to US money. Why? In general, the details surrounding the setup seem rather random, rather than supported by an in-universe reason.

Overall though… my main question here is "why does this happen?" The anomalous blackmail is creepy, sure, but to someone who can spare $10 and the time/energy to make a trip to drop if off, this is just a weird, potentially annoying detour in their regular daily life. The threatening note about the coma just feels, again, predictable: SCPs don't need to be dangerous to be successful.

The hook of "the secret is mysterious" admittedly feels a little lazy to me. It also leads to the question, "what if someone doesn't have any secrets, or doesn't care if their secrets are revealed?"

I feel like for this to be workable, you'd need to do a lot of revisions. For me to be more likely to enjoy the premise, I'd need to know:

  • why is this blackmail scheme happening to begin with?
  • why does the blackmail scheme operate the way it does?
  • where does the money go?
  • how would the Foundation find out about the anomaly in the first place?

Ideally the answers to these questions would work well within the context of an overarching story, rather than just a collection of information bits thrown together conflictingly.

We definitely already have a lot of exchange-based articles on the site (you can use the Tag Search tool to find them). What will make yours unique and memorable?

item.title: Re: Threadmother (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
First of all, a tremendous heap of thanks for the feedback, Monseur Karpin.

I'm definitely going to remove the AI aspect, you're not the first to have a hurdle with it, and as mentioned, it isn't benefitting the story really.

How does a simpler name sound, like "Spinner" or "The Spinner"?

+ show block
– hide block

About the connection to ancient Sumer, the Threadmother is vaguely mentioned or hinted at in a number of religions of Europe and the Middle-East, first of which is Sumer. My idea is that a lot of existing religions have a small and secret cult within them that knows about Threadmother and works to preserve and spread her. Whenever a new religion formed, the cult worked to imbed itself in the new religion. The notions of threads and strands of fate found in a number of religions is the working of the cult. It isn't a necessarily evil or sinister cult, I don't want the story to be that simple.

About the arc of the story, my thought is this: The logs switch between one log from a researcher in a specific field (starting maybe with a Historian, maybe an Acoustic Engineer, etc.), and one log with Francesca. The switching between normal researcher and Francesca serves two purposes, it gives an excuse to add some background information on Threadmother, and it provides a contrast to how Francesca approaches the SCP, and how she manages to achieve results. She starts out slightly aggressive, thinking her research is being put into question. The Foundation has struggled to replicate her achievements with the phenomena, and Francesca feels that her entire methodology and approach is being put into question. She warms up a bit to the interviewer, and shares her process.

She starts to talk a little bit about her childhood, and how Threadmother perceives the world in a way similar to how she did. She hid in her room, behind a closed door, hearing arguments and fights on the other side, but being unable to hear the words. That's how Threadmother senses the world, the vibrations and the tone, but not the words. She later discovers how Threadmother uses a sort of names to distinguish between people, and imbedded in those names is her view on that person. Someone she likes will have a name that consists of very pleasing sounds, while people she dislikes will have names that sound very dissonant. Threadmother communicates in a way where every "word" also has an imbedded feeling, depending on how dissonant or not the sound is.

The arc is the slow exploration of Threadmother and her way of communicating, and even the way in which she connects to Francesca. Many of the events in Francesca life will have mirrors of them in the life of Threadmother. Francesca heard violent fights and arguments as a child, just like Threadmother heard the screaming and jostling of war around her, but without seeing the events directly. They're both scarred, they've got temper, they've got some anger, but they aren't bad or evil.
